item.title: Hospitality Workers Train for Medical Emergencies in Pensacola Area
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Hospitality workers across the Pensacola area are getting equipped with lifesaving emergency response skills through a partnership between Ascension Sacred Heart and Visit Pensacola. The training initiative, held in Perdido Key, aims to prepare hotel, restaurant, and tourism industry employees to recognize and respond quickly to medical…
item.content:encoded:
Hospitality workers across the Pensacola area are getting equipped with lifesaving emergency response skills through a partnership between Ascension Sacred Heart and Visit Pensacola.

The training initiative, held in Perdido Key, aims to prepare hotel, restaurant, and tourism industry employees to recognize and respond quickly to medical emergencies. According to WKRG News 5, the emphasis is on being ready to act decisively when situations arise, whether during peak tourist season or slower months.

Ascension Sacred Heart and Visit Pensacola designed the program to ensure that frontline hospitality staff—who often encounter guests and visitors in vulnerable situations—know basic emergency protocols and can provide immediate assistance before first responders arrive.

The partnership underscores growing recognition in the tourism industry that trained staff can make a critical difference in emergency outcomes. As one of Northwest Florida's major economic engines, the hospitality sector regularly brings thousands of visitors to Pensacola beaches and attractions year-round, making emergency preparedness among workers an ongoing priority.

item.title: Milton Fire Department lands $25K grant for life-saving equipment
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Milton Fire Department has secured more than $25,000 in funding to upgrade its emergency response capabilities. According to a department announcement, MFD received a $25,195 grant through the Firehouse Subs Public Safety Foundation. The funding will go toward purchasing new equipment designed to improve the department's ability to respond to…
item.content:encoded:
The Milton Fire Department has secured more than $25,000 in funding to upgrade its emergency response capabilities. According to a department announcement, MFD received a $25,195 grant through the Firehouse Subs Public Safety Foundation.

The funding will go toward purchasing new equipment designed to improve the department's ability to respond to emergencies and save lives in the Santa Rosa County community. The Firehouse Subs Public Safety Foundation regularly awards grants to fire departments across the country to help them obtain critical gear and technology.

Milton Fire officials said the grant will help ensure the department remains equipped with modern, reliable tools for firefighting and rescue operations.

The closure will span parts of two days, though specific dates and times for the work have not yet been announced. The causeway is a critical corridor for…
item.content:encoded:
Motorists traveling between Pensacola and Mobile should plan for delays as a portion of the I-10 Causeway in Spanish Fort will temporarily close for bridge repair work, according to WKRG News 5.

The closure will span parts of two days, though specific dates and times for the work have not yet been announced. The causeway is a critical corridor for traffic between the Pensacola area and points east, carrying significant daily commuter and commercial traffic.

Drivers are urged to monitor traffic updates and consider using alternate routes during the scheduled closure. Additional details about the exact timing and nature of the bridge repairs are expected to be released as the work date approaches.

item.title: Santa Rosa County Gears Up for 59th Annual Farm Tour
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Santa Rosa County is preparing to welcome visitors back to its annual farm tour, a nearly six-decade-old tradition that showcases the region's agricultural heritage and working farms. The farm tour, now in its 59th year, offers residents and visitors a chance to see local farming operations up close and learn about the crops and livestock that…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County is preparing to welcome visitors back to its annual farm tour, a nearly six-decade-old tradition that showcases the region's agricultural heritage and working farms.

The farm tour, now in its 59th year, offers residents and visitors a chance to see local farming operations up close and learn about the crops and livestock that define the area's rural economy. According to WKRG News 5, the event continues to be a popular draw for those interested in agriculture and rural life in Northwest Florida.

The farm tour has become a staple event for Santa Rosa County, reflecting the importance of agriculture to the local community and providing an educational opportunity for families to connect with the land and farming practices in the region.

IMPACT 100 Pensacola Bay Area has announced its 2026 grant finalists, directing $101,000 in funding to 13 local organizations working on community projects. According to a news release, the grants represent the organization's commitment to supporting charitable work across the Pensacola area.

The selected groups will use the funding to advance various initiatives benefiting residents throughout the region. IMPACT 100 Pensacola Bay Area pools donations from members to award significant grants to vetted nonprofits and community-focused organizations.

The full list of finalist organizations and their specific projects is available through IMPACT 100's announcement. Residents interested in learning more about the grant recipients or the organization's work can contact IMPACT 100 Pensacola Bay Area directly for additional details.

The 5th annual event will feature raffles, giveaways, craft beer, contests, and photo opportunities. According to InWeekly, the fundraiser takes place at Gary's Brewery, located at 208 Newman Ave.

Tickets are available through pensacolajeeps.org for anyone interested in supporting the cause. The event combines community engagement with fundraising, making it a popular gathering for local Jeep enthusiasts and breast cancer advocates alike.

item.title: Social Media Scam Alert: Authorities Warn of Cat in the Hat Scheme
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Law enforcement agencies are sounding the alarm about a growing social media scam that uses AI-generated memes and posts featuring the beloved children's character the Cat in the Hat, according to reporting by Newsweek. The scheme, which began circulating online through social posts and artificially created content, has caught the attention of…
item.content:encoded:
Law enforcement agencies are sounding the alarm about a growing social media scam that uses AI-generated memes and posts featuring the beloved children's character the Cat in the Hat, according to reporting by Newsweek.

The scheme, which began circulating online through social posts and artificially created content, has caught the attention of authorities concerned about how the fraudulent material is being distributed. The use of the iconic Dr. Seuss character appears designed to exploit familiarity and trust among social media users.

Details remain limited on exactly how the scam operates or what financial impact it may have locally, but the warning underscores a growing concern about how artificial intelligence tools are being weaponized in online fraud schemes. Authorities recommend residents be cautious about unsolicited messages and claims that appear suspicious, even when they feature recognizable characters or familiar imagery.

If you encounter suspicious posts or messages related to this scheme, report them to the platform where you saw them and consider filing a complaint with the Federal Trade Commission.

item.title: Community Maritime Park's lesser-known heroes get their due
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: While Quint Studer typically gets top billing in the Community Maritime Park origin story—and understandably so, given his financial backing and public role—a new look at the project's history shines light on the many unsung figures who shaped Pensacola's waterfront transformation. According to reporting by InWeekly, the narrative around the park…
item.content:encoded:
While Quint Studer typically gets top billing in the Community Maritime Park origin story—and understandably so, given his financial backing and public role—a new look at the project's history shines light on the many unsung figures who shaped Pensacola's waterfront transformation.

According to reporting by InWeekly, the narrative around the park has long centered on Studer's high-profile involvement: he funded the effort, weathered public criticism, and claimed victory at election night celebrations at Seville Quarter. That visibility came at a cost, though, and it's overshadowed the contributions of other stakeholders, community organizers, and behind-the-scenes players.

The recognition matters because major civic projects rarely succeed on money and personality alone. The Maritime Park's journey from concept to reality involved countless decisions, relationships, and work by people whose names rarely appear in headlines. Understanding those contributions provides a fuller picture of how Pensacola's downtown waterfront came together—and how similar projects might succeed in the future.

As the park continues to evolve and draw visitors to downtown, acknowledging the broader cast of characters in its creation story helps tell a more complete version of how the city transformed its relationship with the bayfront.

item.title: Pensacola Set to Launch Community Radio Station Ahead of National Conference
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A group of local musicians and radio enthusiasts is preparing to launch a new community-focused radio station just as Pensacola gears up to host the national Grassroots Radio Conference, according to InWeekly. The initiative reflects a broader movement among radio advocates who believe the medium should remain deeply connected to local communities…
item.content:encoded:
A group of local musicians and radio enthusiasts is preparing to launch a new community-focused radio station just as Pensacola gears up to host the national Grassroots Radio Conference, according to InWeekly.

The initiative reflects a broader movement among radio advocates who believe the medium should remain deeply connected to local communities rather than dominated by distant corporate interests. The timing of the station's launch coincides with the conference, which draws participants focused on grassroots broadcasting and independent radio operations.

While details about the station's specific format, frequency, and launch date remain limited, the project underscores Pensacola's growing presence as a hub for alternative media and community-driven broadcasting. Local organizers see the venture as an opportunity to give airtime to voices and music that might otherwise be overlooked by mainstream radio outlets.

The Grassroots Radio Conference will bring national attention to Pensacola's radio community during the conference dates, providing a platform for local broadcasters to connect with peers from across the country who share similar visions for independent, listener-supported programming.

item.title: Escambia County Commission OK's $890M budget amid debate
item.dc:creator: newsroom

The move came during what the publication described as a contentious commission meeting earlier this month. The budget will guide county spending across all departments and services for the fiscal…
item.content:encoded: The Escambia County Commission has adopted a tentative budget of nearly $890.1 million for the upcoming fiscal year 2026/2027, according to InWeekly. The move came during what the publication described as a contentious commission meeting earlier this month. The budget will guide county spending across all departments and services for the fiscal year ahead. County commissioners will have opportunities to make adjustments during the final budget approval process before the fiscal year begins. The commission's adoption of the tentative budget is the first major step in finalizing how the county will allocate its resources for the coming year.

item.title: Barry Secures Millage Rate Cut in Escambia County Budget Vote
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County Commissioner Steven Barry helped push through a millage rate reduction during a contentious budget hearing last week, according to InWeekly. Barry secured the four votes necessary to approve the tax cut, a significant win in what has been a heated debate over county finances. Millage rates directly affect property tax bills for…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County Commissioner Steven Barry helped push through a millage rate reduction during a contentious budget hearing last week, according to InWeekly. Barry secured the four votes necessary to approve the tax cut, a significant win in what has been a heated debate over county finances.

Millage rates directly affect property tax bills for county residents, making the outcome a tangible issue for homeowners across Escambia County. The budget hearing drew considerable attention from commissioners and the public, reflecting the importance stakeholders place on how tax dollars are allocated and collected.

The successful vote marks a rare consensus moment on the Escambia County Commission, where budget decisions often divide board members along competing priorities for schools, infrastructure, and services.

item.title: Pensacola Poet Ericka Streeter Keeps Literary Flame Alive Through Community Workshops
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Ericka Streeter has become a fixture in Pensacola's literary scene, using her work as both personal devotion and community service. The local poet has spent years mentoring Northwest Florida writers through journaling workshops and creative writing sessions, building relationships one stanza at a time. Streeter's commitment to nurturing local…
item.content:encoded:
Ericka Streeter has become a fixture in Pensacola's literary scene, using her work as both personal devotion and community service. The local poet has spent years mentoring Northwest Florida writers through journaling workshops and creative writing sessions, building relationships one stanza at a time.

Streeter's commitment to nurturing local talent extends beyond one-on-one mentorship. She hosted Pensacola Poetry, a community platform for verse and spoken word, for two and a half years—a role that positioned her as a connector between established writers and those just beginning to explore their craft.

According to InWeekly, Streeter approaches her poetry as a form of ancestral worship, weaving family history and cultural threads throughout her work. That same reverence for tradition and connection shapes how she guides other writers, emphasizing journaling and reflection as tools for deeper creative expression.

For local writers looking to develop their skills or connect with Pensacola's literary community, Streeter's workshops and mentorship have provided both technical guidance and encouragement—the kind of grassroots support that keeps a city's cultural scene vibrant.

item.title: Repticon Exotic Animal Expo heading to Fort Walton Beach this October

item.content:encoded:
Reptile enthusiasts and exotic animal lovers in Northwest Florida will have a chance to see snakes, lizards, and other animals up close this fall. According to event organizers, Repticon — an exotic animal exposition — is scheduled for October in Fort Walton Beach, running both Saturday and Sunday.

The traveling Repticon events typically draw crowds interested in learning about and purchasing reptiles and exotic pets, along with related supplies and care products. The Fort Walton Beach show will feature a variety of vendors and educational opportunities for both seasoned collectors and curious newcomers.

While specific dates and venue details weren't fully outlined in the initial announcement, organizers encourage interested visitors to check the Repticon website or local event listings for complete information about times, ticket pricing, and parking. The event's exact location in Fort Walton Beach will be confirmed as the October date approaches.

item.title: 45th Annual MOWA Choctaw Pow Wow Returns to Mount Vernon in October
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Mississippi-Louisiana Choctaw Nation is preparing for its 45th annual pow wow in Mount Vernon, Alabama, scheduled for the first weekend in October. The event will feature traditional drumming, dance performances, and a pageant celebrating Choctaw culture and heritage. The pow wow represents one of the region's longest-running celebrations of…
item.content:encoded:
The Mississippi-Louisiana Choctaw Nation is preparing for its 45th annual pow wow in Mount Vernon, Alabama, scheduled for the first weekend in October. The event will feature traditional drumming, dance performances, and a pageant celebrating Choctaw culture and heritage.

The pow wow represents one of the region's longest-running celebrations of Native American traditions. According to organizers, attendees can expect to experience authentic cultural demonstrations and competitions that have drawn visitors from across the Southeast for nearly five decades.

While Mount Vernon is across the state line in Alabama, the event draws participants and visitors from throughout the Southeast, including from the Florida Panhandle region. Details on specific schedule, admission, and activities are available through event organizers.

item.content:encoded:
A Pensacola comedian is building momentum in the Austin comedy scene after a memorable appearance on "Kill Tony," one of the most popular comedy podcasts in the country. Shane Camp got his shot on the show last month, delivering performances that caught the attention of the show's large audience and fellow comedians.

According to WKRG News 5, Camp's appearance has opened doors in the Austin comedy community, where he's been making connections and carving out space for himself. The podcast, known for its roast-style format and brutal comedy critiques, has become a launching pad for comedians looking to break through in the industry.

Camp's success reflects the growing opportunities for local talent to gain national exposure through digital platforms. For Pensacola's comedy community, his momentum on such a high-profile show could bring more attention to the area's comedy scene.

item.title: Blue Wahoos Face Elimination After Game 1 Loss to Biloxi

The team will need to dig deep as they prepare for the next contest, with no room for error if they hope to advance further in the playoffs. Despite the setback, the Wahoos have had a strong…
item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola Blue Wahoos' season hangs in the balance after dropping their playoff opener to the Biloxi Shuckers, putting their postseason run in jeopardy. The team will need to dig deep as they prepare for the next contest, with no room for error if they hope to advance further in the playoffs.

Despite the setback, the Wahoos have had a strong regular season, posting their third-best winning percentage in franchise history. That consistency throughout the year could serve as a foundation as the team looks to bounce back from the disappointing start to their playoff push.

The Blue Wahoos have built a roster known for its resilience, a quality that will be tested as they face an elimination scenario in what's become a crucial playoff series against Biloxi.

item.title: UWF helps Century residents explore home childcare after daycare closure
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The University of West Florida's Small Business Development Center held a free workshop Tuesday evening in Century aimed at helping residents start their own in-home childcare businesses. The timing comes as the community grapples with the loss of Camp Fire Century Youth Learning Center, which was the only traditional daycare serving the area.…
item.content:encoded:
The University of West Florida's Small Business Development Center held a free workshop Tuesday evening in Century aimed at helping residents start their own in-home childcare businesses. The timing comes as the community grapples with the loss of Camp Fire Century Youth Learning Center, which was the only traditional daycare serving the area.

According to the SBDC, the workshop "Launching a Home-based Childcare Business" provided guidance on starting and operating a childcare business from home—a potential solution as parents in Century search for reliable care options following the closure.

The closure has sparked renewed interest in alternative childcare arrangements across North Escambia County. Home-based providers could help fill the gap left by the daycare's closure and offer flexible options for working families in the Century area.

The UWF Small Business Development Center regularly offers free training and resources to entrepreneurs throughout Northwest Florida. Residents interested in future workshops or business guidance can contact the center through UWF.
